title: Formulary Tier Grandfathering Dispute After P&T Committee Reclassification
scenario_text:
A patient (MRN 4402891 at Vantage Regional, MRN 77-20145 at the former Lakeside campus) has been on Xeljanz 5mg for moderate RA since March 2025. At that time, tofacitinib was Tier 3 (preferred specialty) on the Vantage formulary.

**SharePoint — /pharmacy/formulary/2026-formulary-v2.xlsx (Published Jan 15, 2026)**
Therapeutic Class: JAK Inhibitors | Xeljanz (tofacitinib) | Tier: 4 (Non-preferred specialty) | PA Required: Yes | Step Therapy: Must fail 2 bDMARDs | Effective: Feb 1, 2026
[Document Properties: Last modified by P&T Committee Coordinator, Jan 12, 2026]

**SharePoint — /pharmacy/formulary/policies/grandfathering-policy-v3.docx (Published Sep 2024)**
Section 4.1: "Patients with active PA approvals at the time of a formulary tier change shall be grandfathered at their current tier until their PA expiration date, unless the P&T Committee specifies otherwise."
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @dr.navarro, Jan 8, 2026]: "For the JAK inhibitor reclassification specifically, P&T voted to require re-review at next PA renewal for ALL patients, no grandfathering. This overrides 4.1. Documenting here per Linda's request since the meeting minutes aren't finalized yet."

**Epic Pharmacy Module — Prior Authorization Record**
Patient: [MRN 4402891] | Drug: Tofacitinib 5mg BID | PA Status: Approved | Approved by: Dr. Mehta (Medical Director) | Approval Date: Mar 14, 2025 | Expiration: Mar 14, 2026 | Notes: "Patient failed methotrexate and Humira. Meets UM criteria v2025.1."

**PBM Portal (Express Scripts) — Claim Adjudication Log, Feb 3, 2026**
Rx Claim #EX-9928401 | NDC: 00069-0501-30 | Status: REJECTED | Reason: NDC requires PA — no active PA on file matching current UM criteria | Pharmacy: Vantage Specialty Pharmacy | Reject Code: 75 (Prior Authorization Required)

**Microsoft Teams — Pharmacy Ops Channel (Feb 4, 2026, 8:47 AM)**
@patricia.okonkwo: Getting calls from specialty pharmacy about Xeljanz claims rejecting. Patients had valid PAs. Is this the tier change?
@linda.marsh: Yes. New UM criteria went live Feb 1. PBM is rejecting because the old PA codes don't map to the new tier requirements.
@patricia.okonkwo: But these patients are grandfathered per policy 4.1?
@linda.marsh: (thumbs-down emoji) Not for JAK inhibitors. P&T made an exception. Check the formulary doc comments, I think Rachel documented it there.
@dr.mehta: I approved these originally. Happy to re-review but need the updated criteria. Where are they posted?
[No further replies in thread]
question: Should the patient's Xeljanz claim be processed under the existing PA approval (grandfathered at Tier 3), or must a new PA be submitted under the 2026 UM criteria?

contributor.name: Patricia Okonkwo
contributor.title: Pharmacy Benefits Operations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Formulary management, prior authorization appeals, PBM contract interpretation, step therapy exceptions

choices: Process at Tier 3 under the existing PA; the grandfathering policy (Section 4.1) protects this patient until PA expiration in March 2026
Require a new PA under 2026 UM criteria; the P&T Committee explicitly overrode grandfathering for JAK inhibitors
Process at Tier 4 but without requiring a new PA, since the patient has a valid approval on file regardless of tier placement
Reject and require the patient to restart step therapy (fail 2 bDMARDs) before Xeljanz can be re-authorized
